clue.text: Come running and pull to pieces

definitions.meaning: to arrive in a rush, racing to a place
to rip something such as a letter into shreds

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday phrasal-verb meanings: dashing up somewhere, and ripping paper into shreds.

clue.text: Part of the country is against ale brewing

indicators.note: brewing stirs and works up its ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A region of England is said to oppose the brewing of ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewing' mixes AGAINST and ALE together; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: East Anglia is a region of eastern England, so it is one part of the country.

clue.text: Sticky stuff used by agents to catch a fool

indicators.note: agents catching a fool hold that fool inside their own letters

parts.note: moles are spies, secret agents planted inside an organisation
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Spies use something sticky as bait to trap an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle-like syrup from sugar refining is a thick and sticky substance.

clue.text: I have a dog

definitions.meaning: the person who compiled this crossword refers to themselves
a breed of gun dog, such as the Irish or English one

explanation.definitionFit: The compiler of a crossword is its setter, and setters are also a breed of gun dog.

clue.text: This will help you to sleep soundly, said easterner

definitions.text: This will help you to sleep

indicators.note: soundly, beside sleep, also signals that the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: said plus Asian, a person from the East, run together when spoken

explanation.surface: A sleeping aid recommended by someone from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' seems to describe the sleep but tells you to say 'said Asian' out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedation is the administering of a calming drug that makes a patient drowsy and sleep.

clue.text: Weak prescription to treat paw injury?

indicators.note: an injury damages and twists the shape of things, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A vet offers a feeble remedy for an animal's hurt paw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injury' rearranges TREAT and PAW together; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Water from the tap is a joking stand-in for a placebo, a medicine with no strength at all.

clue.text: French leader's refusal to entertain a fellow European

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: non is the French for no, a refusal fitting a French leader
a Pole is a person from Poland, a fellow European

explanation.surface: The French emperor declines to host someone from another European country.
explanation.walkthrough: The refusal is French, matching the French leader: NON opens up to hold A POLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was the French emperor and military leader of the early nineteenth century.

clue.text: What may be heard from the choir?

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the run of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A question about the sound that comes out of a church choir.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound is something heard after the original noise, a repeat bouncing back.

clue.text: Party leader at international organisation turns up without cover

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading the joined pieces from the bottom upward

parts.note: Ed Miliband led the Labour Party when this puzzle appeared
UN is the United Nations

explanation.surface: A politician arrives at a global body without any clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses the whole of ED and UN, giving the down entry read upward; 'at' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nude is naked, with no clothing or covering at all.

clue.text: Model violated when about to leave

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for violated is read backwards

parts.note: raped means violated
the Model T was Ford's famous early motor car

explanation.surface: A model is assaulted just as she is about to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns RAPED into DEPAR; 'when' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to go away from a place, a synonym of leave.

clue.text: Suffered discomfort after a race, but hung on

indicators.note: after places the word for suffered discomfort following the other pieces

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race
ached means suffered discomfort

explanation.surface: Someone in pain after running a race nevertheless held on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something attached is fixed on or fastened, hung onto something else.

clue.text: Tracks crossing the river where people jump

indicators.note: the tracks cross over the river, so they go around it

parts.note: tramlines are the rails a tram runs on
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: Railway lines run over a river at a spot where people leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Trampolines are springy sheets of fabric on frames that gymnasts and children bounce on.

clue.text: Volume containing a true array of writing

indicators.note: containing means the volume word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a litre is a measure of volume

indicators.note: an array is an arrangement, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A book holds a genuine collection of written material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'array' rearranges A TRUE, and those letters sit inside the volume word; 'of' is a link word. The surface reads 'Volume' as a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature is written work, especially books valued as art.

clue.text: Figure out place to have sex

indicators.note: to figure out a thing is to work it out, and here the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tries to work out a location for a romantic encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure out' looks like one phrase meaning solve, but only 'Figure' is the signal; 'out' is part of the mix with PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To copulate is to mate, a formal word for having intercourse.

clue.text: Godless found at armed robberies?

parts.note: heists are robberies, often armed

explanation.surface: Unbelievers turn up at scenes of holdups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is a link word; the definition is an adjective used as a noun, the godless.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheists are people who deny that any god exists, the godless ones.

clue.text: Ham is above the law

parts.note: over means above
an act is a law passed by a parliament

explanation.surface: A piece of meat is said to be beyond legal reach.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform with exaggeration on stage, a verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Shrewdly, as a follower of Robin Hood

parts.note: Will Stutely was one of Robin Hood's band of Merry Men in the ballads

explanation.surface: Acting cleverly, in the manner of one of the outlaws of Sherwood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word; Stutely is a lesser-known member of the legendary outlaw band.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting astutely means acting with sharp judgement, cleverly and shrewdly.

clue.text: City call to spend?

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
to shout is to call out loudly

explanation.surface: A city summons people to go shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; to lash out is British informal for spending money freely.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out is to spend money lavishly, splurging on something.

clue.text: Savour impertinence from sailors?

indicators.note: from places the source, the sailors, before the impertinence in the answer

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, and two of them make the plural
sauce is cheek or impertinence

explanation.surface: Enjoy the cheek of seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sailors' gives two TARs; tartare sauce is the mayonnaise relish served with fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauce adds relish to food, so savour here is the tasty relish itself.

clue.text: Frugal type puts in a pound for the plate

indicators.note: the frugal type puts the pound inside itself

parts.note: a saver is someone thrifty
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A thrifty person drops a pound coin on the collection plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A salver is a flat tray, typically silver, for serving drinks or letters.

clue.text: Spare wound

definitions.meaning: British slang for surplus or unwanted
a long deep cut in the flesh

explanation.definitionFit: Gash is slang for surplus, and also a deep cut in skin.

clue.text: Stimulus is false without promises

indicators.note: without means the promises are taken away from the word for false

parts.note: spurious means false or fake
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: Motivation is phoney when no pledges are given.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is anything that urges on, a goad or incentive.

clue.text: Lust like a Cockney saying he's jolly drunk?

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the initial h, so the words are spoken that way

parts.note: happy and tight, both meaning merry and drunk, with the h dropped

explanation.surface: Desire as a London tippler would describe being merrily drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner who drops his aitches; 'he's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is a strong desire or craving, close to lust.

clue.text: Ship's boat turns in, as for good

indicators.note: in puts the turned boat inside the other word
turns means the boat word is read backwards

parts.note: a yawl is a ship's small boat

explanation.surface: A dinghy capsizes, which is permanent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses the boat; the surface reads 'turns in' as a boat capsizing, but 'in' is the container signal and 'as' gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Always means forever or permanently, the meaning of for good.

clue.text: Harry led astray by the arms?

indicators.note: led astray means sent the wrong way, so the letters go out of order

explanation.surface: Harry is misled by someone holding his arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldry is the study and art of coats of arms.

clue.text: Cuts 23 on board

annotationWithheld.why: Cuts 23 on board (6): the only parse has 'on board' both giving SS (steamship) and signalling that EVER goes inside it, one phrase doing two jobs
